newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end dull trading firmer.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end dull trading firmer.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended a session of very light range-trading mostly firmer.
Traders bemoaned the lack of followthrough in either direction and said scanty morning order flows never picked up, leaving futures stranded inside very tight price bands.
"I'm bored silly," said one bank floor broker. "We had a 14-point range in the D-mark."

Some said the currency market was continuing to digest last Friday's mixed September U.S. employment report, which elicited conflicting reactions about whether the Federal Reserve might need to tighten credit in November.
Traders agreed the main feature on Monday was the yen's advance on the crosses and against the U.S. unit after Japanese politicians overnight said Japanese rates might rise.

A senior official of Japan's Liberal Democratic Party was quoted by a U.S. news agency as saying on Monday that a rise in the Japanese official discount rate will probably be considered after the October 20 general election.
Separately, the head of Japan's main opposition party said the country's interest rate levels must be corrected.
"You have to just believe they're (Japan) going to raise before Europe is going to lower them," said another broker.
